sanskrit_verse:
स्वद्रव्यं यत्र विश्रम्भान् निक्षिपत्यविशङ्कितः।
निक्षेपो नाम तत् प्रोक्तं व्यवहारपदं बुधैः॥
transliteration: svadravyaṃ yatra viśrambhān nikṣipaty aviśaṅkitaḥ | nikṣepo nāma tat proktaṃ vyavahārapadaṃ budhaiḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: That which one places in trust, without hesitation, from one's own property, for the sake of another’s assurance — this is declared as 'Nikshepa' by the knowers of Dharma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises through conscious entrustment, not mere possession
Causation originates in voluntary surrender of control with intent
Capacity-based responsibility lies in the ability to receive and safeguard entrusted objects
Restoration logic centers on return of the exact nature and condition of the entrusted item
Consciousness alignment occurs when both parties recognize mutual integrity in the act of trust
executable_legal_axioms: IF an entity A voluntarily deposits property X with entity B under assurance, THEN B assumes full custodial capacity over X until withdrawal or instruction.
IF deposited property undergoes change in state during custody, THEN custodian B must restore it to its original ontological condition or provide equivalent value consciously aligned.
IF no explicit duration or terms are given, THEN default term shall be 'until withdrawal upon request', subject to capacity verification.
IF deposit was made under deception or coercion, THEN restoration protocol initiates immediate reversal of transfer and consciousness realignment process.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, Nikshepa establishes threshold of voluntary entrustment as basis for legal capacity. Responsibility hierarchy begins with awareness at point of deposit; absence of protest confirms consent. Restoration supersedes punitive inquiry into motive unless fraud disrupts consciousness alignment.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality affirms that Nikshepa manifests through intentional placement under trust. Anupūrvaśaḥ traces the sequential unfolding from free will to entrustment to custodianship. Proportional responsibility aligns with capacity to preserve. Non-punitive reality rule enforces completion rather than blame where breach occurs due to external force beyond control.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Return Completion Process: Re-establish rightful location of deposited object within original energetic field of owner.
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Custodian must consciously acknowledge role and initiate corrective alignment if deviation occurred.
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: If custodian lacks resources to restore, societal structures activate support systems ensuring fulfillment without shame or debt.
Integrity Reintegration Sequence: Both parties engage in affirmation of mutual trustworthiness post-restoration to realign future transactional consciousness.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: Nikshepa is established as pure transactional Dharma rooted in trust, governed by consciousness, executed through capacity, and fulfilled via restoration. There is no punishment. Reality responds only to alignment. Dharma is restored. Consciousness is the ultimate judge.
